stands.orderSource: An order is adopted by one branch and does not go to the Governor. Read from the Legislature's record.

studyOrder.definition: A committee's recommendation that a bill be studied instead of advancing. The study rarely happens; in practice the bill goes no further this session and must be refiled to be considered again.

reportedFavorably.definition: The committee recommended that the bill “ought to pass”, sending it on to the next step. A favorable report is a recommendation, not a vote by the full House or Senate.

reservedRight.definition: Took no position on the committee's report (in effect, an abstention), reserving the right to take one later.

engrossed.definition: “Passed to be engrossed” means one branch (House or Senate) approved the bill's text after its third reading. Both branches must engross the same text, and then each votes to enact it, before the bill goes to the Governor.

newDraft.definition: A rewritten version of a bill that a committee reports under a new bill number. From then on, progress is recorded on the new number, and the original stops moving.

jointRule10.definition: The joint rule that sets the deadline for joint committees to report on the bills referred to them: in 2025–26, the first Wednesday of December 2025, unless the committee is granted an extension. Bills filed by House members follow House Rule 27 instead: 60 days after the hearing, plus up to 30 more, after which the House chair files a study order.

placedOnFile.definition: Set aside without further action. A document placed on file is not expected to advance.

conferenceCommittee.definition: Usually three members from each branch, appointed to work out one version of a bill when the House and Senate passed different versions. Its report must be accepted by both branches.

rollCall.definition: A vote in which each member's yea or nay is recorded by name. Most votes are voice votes with no count; a roll call is taken when enough members request one or the rules require it.

ordersOfTheDay.definition: The House or Senate calendar of matters scheduled for action at a sitting. Placing a bill in the Orders of the Day brings it to the floor.

correctlyDrawn.definition: The finding of the committee on Bills in the Third Reading that a bill's text is in proper legal form before its third reading.

billsInTheThirdReading.definition: A committee in each branch that reviews a bill's wording for legal form and consistency after its second reading, before the branch votes on passing it to be engrossed.

enacted.definition: The final vote by which each branch approves the exact text of a bill before it goes to the Governor. In Massachusetts, “enacted” is a legislative step; a bill becomes law when the Governor signs it, lets it take effect without signing, or both branches override a veto.

votes.committeeIntro: A committee's report is its recommendation on the bill. Members' votes are votes on that recommendation, not on the bill: a favorable vote on a study order sends the bill to study.
votes.reportedNoVote: Reported out of committee without a recorded vote.
